# native/vendor/

GPUI (`gpui-pre`, a weekly snapshot of Zed's gpui) and gpui-kit with its component crates, and AccessKit's `accesskit_consumer`, `accesskit_atspi_common`, `accesskit_macos` and `accesskit_windows` (patched, below), as the exact crates.io tarballs that `native/Cargo.lock` resolves for `gpui-kit = "=0.10.0"` (which pins `gpui-pre = "=0.3.12"`). They are wired into the workspace by `[patch.crates-io]` in `native/Cargo.toml` and are not workspace members (`exclude = ["draw", "vendor"]`), so `native/check.sh` does not format or lint them.

The commit that adds each folder holds its tarball untouched (the GPUI family in one commit, each AccessKit crate in a later one): each folder is the tarball's contents with the leading `<crate>-<version>/` stripped, licence files where the tarball has them. Every change after that is its own commit, listed under Patches below, so an upgrade is: replace each folder with the new tarball in one commit, then re-apply the list.

To check a folder against its tarball: download the URL, check its sha256, unpack it, and `diff -r` the unpacked folder with this one at the first commit.

`gpui-kit` 0.10.0's tarball carries no licence file; its `Cargo.toml` declares Apache-2.0. `gpui-kit-assets` carries only `LICENSE-LUCIDE` (the icons) and declares Apache-2.0.

## What the public export's scan flags here

The public export's text scan (it refuses a tree that holds a machine's name, a personal path or the shape of a key) flags two upstream lines in this folder, so they are settled before a public export includes it:

| File | Line | What the scan sees | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gpui-base/src/scrollable_mask.rs` | 575 | a laptop model's name | a code comment about its touchpad |
| `gpui-pre-reqwest/src/tls.rs` | 784 | the header line of a PEM key | a test key inside a unit test of the TLS identity parser |

One file under this folder was tracked and ignored at once: `gpui-pre-reqwest/Cargo.lock` is in the crate's tarball, and the tarball's own `.gitignore` named it, so a `git add -A` of an exported copy of the tree dropped it. The line `Cargo.lock` is removed from `gpui-pre-reqwest/.gitignore` (the one ignore file under this folder) and the lock stays, as the other thirty crates' locks stay: every folder here is its tarball's contents. No build reads any of these locks: the crates are path dependencies of `native/`'s workspace, which resolves from `native/Cargo.lock` alone.

Each row is one commit after the untouched import; re-apply them in this order after an upgrade.

| # | Crate | What | Why | Upstream | Files |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | gpui-pre | `A11ySubtreeBuilder::push_descendant` (a synthetic node under another synthetic node) and `A11ySubtreeBuilder::set_focus` (a synthetic node as the focused node) | A link inside a paragraph is a `Link` node holding its own text run, both synthetic; its focusable box has no node, so the paragraph names the link as focused | none filed | `src/window/a11y.rs` |
| 2 | gpui-pre | `Window::activate_a11y_for_test` and `Window::dispatch_a11y_action_for_test`, with `test-support` only | The test platform has no adapter, so no tree is ever built under `TestAppContext`; these let `cargo test` check the accessibility tree and its actions on every host without a window | none filed | `src/window.rs`, `src/window/a11y.rs` |
| 3 | accesskit_consumer | `Node::supports_text_ranges` is also true for `Paragraph`, `Heading`, `Code`, `Cell`, `ColumnHeader` and `RowHeader` nodes that hold text runs | Upstream offers text ranges (the AT-SPI Text interface, AX text ranges, the UIA Text pattern) only on text inputs, `Label`, `Document` and `Terminal`; a chat's paragraphs, headings, code and cells need them to be read by character, word and line | none filed; upstream main unchanged on 2026-11-17 | `src/text.rs` |
| 4 | accesskit_atspi_common | A disabled node is neither `enabled` nor `sensitive` on AT-SPI (it was `enabled` unless it supported read-only) | A disabled Send button read as enabled to Orca; backport of upstream's fix | AccessKit PR #788 (merged 2026-09-01, after 0.19.1) | `src/node.rs` |
| 5 | gpui-pre | `Window::a11y_tree_update_for_test`, with `test-support` only | Tests read the whole `TreeUpdate` (bounds, disabled, busy, live, URLs, text runs) through `accesskit_consumer` as an adapter does; the debug JSON leaves those out | none filed | `src/window.rs`, `src/window/a11y.rs`, `src/window/a11y/debug.rs` |
| 6 | accesskit_atspi_common | A node with `expanded` is `expandable` and `expanded` or `collapsed` on AT-SPI; a busy node is `busy` (state changes are emitted by the existing state diff) | The adapter mapped neither: a fold or tool row read as a plain button and a streaming transcript as idle | none filed; upstream main still lacks both on 2026-11-17 | `src/node.rs` |
| 7 | accesskit_atspi_common | A heading's level is its `level` attribute on AT-SPI (AccessKit's level plus 1: AccessKit counts levels and positions from 0, as `accesskit_windows` shows by adding 1 to both) | The adapter exported no level, so Orca could not say "heading level 2" | none filed; upstream main lacks it on 2026-11-17 | `src/node.rs` |
| 8 | gpui-pre-macos | `GPUIView` answers `accessibilityFocusedUIElement` by asking its superview (the content view AccessKit subclasses), so the app's AXFocusedUIElement is the focused node instead of the window and VoiceOver follows Tab focus | (from gate-mac, branch s4-gate-mac commit 02c966a5) | none filed | `src/window.rs` |
| 9 | gpui-pre | A reused cached view puts back its previous frame's accessibility nodes (as the top of its subtree under the current node), their focus ids, bounds and action listeners, and the focus when the focused element is among them; `PrepaintStateIndex` records the node count around each view's prepaint | Zed #66690: every node under a cached view vanished from the tree on the frames that reused it, with its actions | Zed issue #66690 | `src/window.rs`, `src/window/a11y.rs` |
| 10 | gpui-base | A text selection that starts in a markdown table cell is no longer confined to the cell (the cell is not recorded as the anchor cell, so `confine_to_cell` never applies) | Decided for the app (gate-mac FOR-GATE 11): a drag from a cell runs on past the table as in a browser; upstream confines it on purpose. The chat transcript draws its own text and selection (`mcbench-ui` `view/text_leaf.rs`), so this governs gpui-base's TextView elsewhere | not upstream: a behaviour choice | `src/text/node.rs` |
| 11 | gpui-base | A multi-line input's text runs get bounds and character geometry (from the last layout, when it lays out every line from the first and holds this text), split where a line wraps, with a text direction; an assistive client's `SetTextSelection` sets the input's caret and selection | The composer's runs had no geometry (VoiceOver's and Orca's cursor and character boxes at the screen's corner, gate-mac FOR-GATE 13) and `set_caret_offset`/`set_selection` did nothing | none filed | `src/input/base/a11y_text.rs`, `src/input/base/state.rs` |
| 12 | accesskit_atspi_common, accesskit_unix | The AT-SPI EditableText interface on text inputs (`SetTextContents` becomes AccessKit's `SetValue`) | Without it an AT-SPI client cannot set the composer's text; backport of upstream's PR, applied with its paths mapped to these folders | AccessKit PR #779 | `accesskit_atspi_common/src/node.rs`, `accesskit_atspi_common/src/simplified.rs`, `accesskit_unix/src/atspi/bus.rs`, `accesskit_unix/src/atspi/interfaces/editable_text.rs`, `accesskit_unix/src/atspi/interfaces/mod.rs` |
| 13 | gpui-pre-wgpu | A variable font (one face in fontdb, at its default weight) gets an instance at each requested weight: shaped with that weight, measured and rasterized with its `wght` axis there; the scale context's coordinates are replaced for every glyph | The bold-on-Linux defect: GNOME's Adwaita Sans and Inter Variable are variable fonts, every face was loaded at weight 400 and drawn without variation coordinates, so bold, semibold and medium drew as regular (`mcbench-ui` `tests/bold.rs` draws the same picture for 400, 620 and 700 without this patch); swash's `variations` keeps the previous glyph's coordinates for axes it does not name | none filed | `src/cosmic_text_system.rs` |
